parsed.modern: Heatsburg—Of the weights, 122 drachmes = 32 lots = 16 oz. = 2 marks = 1 lb. = 1.0682 lb. avoirdupois; 112 lbs. = 8 lispunds = 1 centner = 119.64 lbs. avoirdupois; and 5 centners = 2 shipfunds. Ten lbs. = 1 stone of wool or feathers = half a stone of flax. Of butter, 280 lbs. form the great, and 24 the small tonne. A pipe of oil is reckoned at 820 lbs. Gold and silver are weighed by the Cologne mark, and their fineness valued as explained under the head Germany. Of measures, 6 palms = 2 feet = 1 ell = 22.78 Brit. inches. The Rhinland foot of engineers and surveyors = 12.30 Brit. inches. The Brabant ell, commonly used for piece goods, = 27.85 Brit. inches. Also 100 quarters = 40 stubgens = 40 stubgens = 20 viertels = 5 eimers = 4 ankers = 1 ahm = 31.87 Brit. gall. and 24 ankers or 6 ahms = 1 fuder. Of wine, 6 tierces = 4 oxhofts or hogsheads = 1 faas; but these are of various sizes. Of corn, 160 spints = 40 himtens = 20 fias = 10 scheffels = 1 wisp or wispel = 25 Brit. bushels; two wisps = 1 last of barley or oats = 7.25 Brit. quarters; and 3 wisps = 1 last of wheat or rye = 1 stock of barley or oats = 10.87 Brit. quarters.
